source_name: K&H Csoport — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: KBC-owned top-3 Hungarian bank; Hungarian-language employer posts and appointment announcements ('új vezetőnk', 'csatlakozott csapatunkhoz') plus headcount curve.

source_name: Erste Magyarország — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Erste Hungary local page — Hungarian-language hiring campaigns, digital/payments team build-outs and executive welcome posts.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Hungary — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: RBI subsidiary; page mixes hu/en posts on organisational changes and hiring, and employee profiles surface role changes early.

source_name: OTP Mobil (SimplePay) — LinkedIn company page (hypothesised slug)
why_relevant: OTP Mobil operates SimplePay, the largest Hungarian online payment gateway; its separate LinkedIn presence tracks payments-specific hiring distinct from OTP Bank's banking headcount.

source_name: LinkedIn Hungarian-language self-announcement post corpus ('örömmel osztom meg')
why_relevant: The canonical Hungarian phrase used by executives to announce their own appointment, often weeks before any employer press release. Search-based monitoring of this phrase plus a bank/fintech term is the highest-yield weak-signal capture in this cell. Confirmed live: a search on this phrase surfaced an OTP Bank profile announcing a move to a Ministry of Finance deputy-state-secretary role.

source_name: LinkedIn Hungarian-language self-announcement corpus ('csatlakoztam' / 'új kihívás')
why_relevant: Second high-yield Hungarian announcement idiom ('csatlakoztam a ... csapatához'). Complements 'örömmel osztom meg' and catches moves phrased retrospectively.

source_name: LinkedIn English-language announcement corpus ('excited to join' + Budapest/bank)
why_relevant: Hungarian executives at international subsidiaries (Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, Citi, Revolut, Wise) post in English; the English idiom set is disjoint from the Hungarian one and must be monitored in parallel.

source_name: Open-web index of LinkedIn posts (site:linkedin.com/posts) as an unauthenticated proxy
why_relevant: A meaningful share of LinkedIn public posts is search-engine indexed, giving a login-free window into the same announcement corpus. Confirmed working: a general web search on the Hungarian phrase returned real linkedin.com/posts and /in/ URLs.

source_name: LinkedIn Jobs — Hungary banking/payments postings
why_relevant: Job postings by the same employers reveal team build-outs (e.g. instant-payments, AML, core-banking migration) before any announcement; volume and role mix over time is a hiring-direction time series.

source_name: FinTechZone — LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Hungarian fintech trade-media page that amplifies and comments on Hungarian fintech/payments personnel moves; an efficient snowball hub for discovering the executives worth following individually.

source_name: OTP Bank — official X account (@otpbank_hu)
why_relevant: Corporate X account; low volume in Hungary but occasionally carries appointment and org announcements ahead of the newsroom, and confirms attribution when a personal post is ambiguous.

source_name: OTP Bank — official Facebook page
why_relevant: Highest-reach Hungarian corporate social channel; employer-branding and recruitment campaigns appear here in Hungarian, useful as a hiring-intensity proxy even though executive moves are rarer.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank — official Facebook page (jegybank)
why_relevant: The central bank posts leadership transitions on this page (a post thanking the outgoing governor was visible in results); MNB deputy-governor and executive-director appointments reshape supervisory counterparties for every bank and payments firm.

source_name: LinkedIn personal profiles of Hungarian banking/payments executives (curated watchlist)
why_relevant: The individual profile is the primary record of a move — title and employer change on the profile itself, often silently, before or instead of any post. A maintained watchlist of ~100 profiles across OTP, MBH, K&H, Erste, Raiffeisen, UniCredit, CIB, Gránit, MNB, Barion, OTP Mobil gives direct role-change detection. Confirmed live examples surfaced in search across MBH, MNB, Raiffeisen and OTP.

source_name: LinkedIn Pulse / long-form posts by Hungarian fintech figures
why_relevant: Self-published Hungarian long-form on the fintech sector maps companies, founders and career histories — a rich actor-map and alias source, and its comment threads reveal who is currently where.

source_name: Hungarian banking/payments recruiter and HR-consultancy LinkedIn accounts
why_relevant: Executive-search and HR consultants publish mandates and placements in Hungarian ('vezetői pozíciót keresünk', 'gratulálunk az új szerepkörhöz'), leaking hiring intent before postings and confirming moves after them.

source_name: Gránit Bank / Gránit Asset Management — LinkedIn presence
why_relevant: Gránit is the fastest-growing Hungarian-owned digital bank; its staff self-announcements (a private-banker appointment surfaced directly in search) are a leading indicator of its private-banking and digital build-out.

source_name: Profession.hu (largest HU job board) - banking/finance & IT categories
why_relevant: Hungary's dominant general job board; nearly every HU bank, processor and BPO posts here. Volume and role-title mix per employer is the earliest demand signal for programmes (core banking migration, instant payment/AFR, AML).

source_name: Profession.hu employer profile pages (company-level vacancy roll-up)
why_relevant: Stable per-employer IDs give a clean time series of open-role counts per bank without name-matching noise - ideal for tracking hiring bursts at MBH, UniCredit, OTP etc.

source_name: CVonline.hu (Alma Career / CV-Online Hungary)
why_relevant: Second major HU board, strong in white-collar finance/compliance roles and in agency-posted (unnamed employer) mandates - agency ads often reveal confidential bank programmes before they are announced.

source_name: Jobline.hu (HVG group job board) - status: announced shutdown
why_relevant: Historically a major HVG-owned white-collar board; reporting found in search states operations cease 31 Jan 2026, so it is at best an archival/back-fill source. Must be validated, not assumed live.

source_name: HVG Allasborze (Jobline job fair) exhibitor lists
why_relevant: Twice-yearly national career fair; the exhibitor roster and the roles each bank/fintech advertises there is a compact, dated snapshot of who is in growth mode.

source_name: Workania.hu (Profesia/Alma group HU board)
why_relevant: Third-tier but regionally connected board (SK/CZ background per HR Portal history); useful for shared-service-centre and back-office banking roles outside Budapest.

source_name: K&H Bank career portal (karrier.kh.hu)
why_relevant: KBC-owned top-5 HU bank; own vacancy list is the authoritative feed for its digital/payments and compliance hiring.

source_name: MBH Bank career page (post-merger entity)
why_relevant: MBH is the merged MKB/Budapest Bank/Takarek group - integration programmes (core migration, branch network rationalisation) show up as role clusters before public announcements.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Hungary career portal (raiffeisen.karrierportal.hu)
why_relevant: Top-5 HU bank vacancy feed; also a concrete example of the Nexum 'Karrier Portál' ATS whose URL pattern (<brand>.karrierportal.hu/allasok) generalises to many HU financial employers.

source_name: Nexum 'Karrier Portál' ATS tenant family (*.karrierportal.hu)
why_relevant: A single HU ATS vendor hosts many bank/financial career sites (Raiffeisen, GIRO, legacy MKB observed). Enumerating its tenants yields a ready-made list of collectable, uniformly structured vacancy feeds.

source_name: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) careers + subsidiary offers pages
why_relevant: Central bank hiring (payment system specialists, supervisors) signals regulatory workload shifts; the 'Leányvállalatok ajánlatai' page is a pointer to GIRO, BSE and other subsidiary vacancy feeds.
